messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Serialise app
parts:
I am not aware of a technique out there for that. But moving to the shiny-discuss list since this is more of a general purpose shiny question. 

On Monday, November 2, 2015, Laurent Gatto <lauren...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear all,

Let's assume I have a list that contains a ui and a server

ui <- fluiPage(...)
server <- function(input, output, session) { ... }
app <- list(ui = ui, server = server)

that then can successfully be executed with runApp(app).

Is there a way to serialise that app, i.e. to create a directory containing ui.R (or www/index.html) and server.R, so that it is possible to subsequently execute runApp("./mySerialisedApp") and obtain the same app as runApp(app) above?

Thank you very much in advance.

Best wishes,

Laurent

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Serialise app
parts:
Not sure if this is a recommended way of doing this, but it might work: in the `mySerialisedApp.R` file, you can return a Shiny app object, like this:

mySerialisedApp.R
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage("I'm a shiny app")
server <- function(input, output, session) {}

shinyApp(ui, server)

And when you want to run it from a different file, you could `source()` , which will return the Shiny app as an object, so you could do

source("mySerialisedApp.R")$value

I think that'd work. Hopefully that's what you were looking for.



As I said, I don't know how encouraged this solution is, so use at your own risk.

Dear Dean,

Thank you very much for your reply.

I was hoping for a solution that could use the app variable directly, rather than a file, to recreate a new app directory. To give you a bit of context, the aim is to use this in the frame of a package, and enable users to create their own app directories (that they could upload to shinyapps.io) using an existing app from that package as template. I wanted to use the app variable, and avoid duplicating code, or having to source the R file in the package.

Best wishes,

Laurent
